params.body:
The trend page says how many signals and sources a trend rests on, and of what kind, but not from where. Breadth across regions is the strongest thing a trend can show, and it is measured. This adds one line under the counts:

> From sources in 6 regions on 3 continents: DACH, Benelux, France, UK / Ireland, North America and East Asia.

## What changes

- `TrendCard::originLine()` builds the line from `reading.origin`, which the pipeline sends (gentells-pipeline, `trend-origin.mjs`): the regions of the Gentells Standard, counted from the country an adapter asked for or the one region a source names, never from the classifier's tags. "on N continents" only when there is more than one. A trend from one region says so plainly ("From sources in DACH."). Nothing known, no line.
- `trend-detail.blade.php`: the line under the kinds line, for every reader. It travels in the reading, so the API and MCP tools carry `origin` too.

Until the pipeline side is deployed, `reading.origin` is absent and the page is unchanged.

## Tests

New `TrendOriginTest`: regions and continents in the line, one region, nothing known, the page shows it to a signed-out reader. The full suite passes apart from BuildStampTest, which fails in any worktree.
params.title: Say where a trend's signals come from, by region
